# Op-ed - From Inside The House: How Surveillance Tech Further Threatens Independent Living

[Privacy & Data](https://cdt.org/area-of-focus/privacy-data/)

## Op-ed – From Inside The House: How Surveillance Tech Further Threatens Independent Living

July 1, 2026
/
[Ariana Aboulafia](https://cdt.org/staff/ariana-aboulafia/)

*The following op-ed authored by Ariana Aboulafia first appeared in Disability Culture Currents on June 30, 2026. A excerpt of the text has been pasted below.*

Independent living is under attack from all sides.

On June 18, 2026, the Department of Justice [released a memo](https://www.justice.gov/olc/media/1446701/dl) undermining decades of precedent surrounding the right of disabled people to live in our communities. The Supreme Court established these rights in the 1999 landmark decision of [Olmstead v. LC](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/527/581/), which found that, under the [Americans with Disabilities Act](https://www.ada.gov/), people with disabilities have the right to receive community-based services in the home of our choice, as opposed to being segregated into institutions. This integration mandate has become one of the cornerstones of the disability rights movement and the independent living movement, often encapsulated by the rallying cry of “[Our homes, not nursing homes](https://nonprofitquarterly.org/disabled-protesters-in-dc-our-homes-not-nursing-homes/).” Independent living means more than living at home; the movement also focuses on autonomy, agency, and freedom of choice, which is one reason why this memo is so concerning to disability activists.

While the DOJ memo — reportedly driven by [Stephen Miller](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/us-law-week/stephen-miller-said-to-drive-doj-memo-eroding-disability-rights) — marks a direct attack on the basic rights of people with disabilities to live our own lives, policies that threaten independent living have multiplied throughout Trump’s second term. The recent cuts to [Medicaid](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/how-people-with-disabilities-will-bear-the-burden-of-medicaid-funding-cuts) will be felt disproportionately by disabled people, and a recent presidential [executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/07/ending-crime-and-disorder-on-americas-streets/) encouraging the [institutionalization of people experiencing homelessness](https://www.urban.org/urban-wire/new-trump-policies-targeting-homelessness-threaten-rights-people-disabilities) with mental health disabilities will fast-track disabled people into institutions instead of connecting us with housing and care solutions. Further, the Trump administration is [working on a rule revision](https://www.propublica.org/article/trump-social-security-ssi-disability-benefits-cuts-parents-children?utm_source=sailthru&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=majorinvestigations&utm_content=feature) that would slash or completely end the benefits of low-income recipients of Supplemental Security Income (SSI), severely harming disabled people who live at home with low-income relatives.

[Read the full op-ed.](https://www.disabilityculturelab.org/posts/from-inside-the-house-how-surveillance-tech-further-threatens-independent-living)

# 評論 - 來自屋內：監控科技如何進一步威脅自立生活

[隱私與資料](https://cdt.org/area-of-focus/privacy-data/)

## 評論 – 來自屋內：監控科技如何進一步威脅自立生活

2026 年 7 月 1 日
/
[Ariana Aboulafia](https://cdt.org/staff/ariana-aboulafia/)

*以下由 Ariana Aboulafia 撰寫的評論文章，最早於 2026 年 6 月 30 日刊登在 Disability Culture Currents。下方摘錄部分內文。*

自立生活正受到四面八方的攻擊。

2026 年 6 月 18 日，美國司法部[發布一份備忘錄](https://www.justice.gov/olc/media/1446701/dl)，削弱了數十年來圍繞障礙者在我們社區中生活權利所建立的判例基礎。美國最高法院在 1999 年具有里程碑意義的 [Olmstead v. LC](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/527/581/) 判決中確立了這些權利；該判決認定，依據[《美國身心障礙者法》](https://www.ada.gov/)，障礙者有權在自己選擇的家中接受以社區為基礎的服務，而不是被隔離到機構裡。這項融合要求已成為障礙權利運動與自立生活運動的基石之一，常被凝聚成一句倡議口號：「[要我們的家，不要護理之家](https://nonprofitquarterly.org/disabled-protesters-in-dc-our-homes-not-nursing-homes/)」。自立生活不只是住在家裡；這場運動同時關注自主、主體性與選擇自由，這也是為什麼這份備忘錄會讓障礙權利倡議者如此憂心的原因之一。

儘管據稱由[史蒂芬・米勒（Stephen Miller）](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/us-law-week/stephen-miller-said-to-drive-doj-memo-eroding-disability-rights)主導的司法部（DOJ）備忘錄，已經是對身心障礙者自主生活基本權利的直接攻擊，但在川普第二任期內，威脅自立生活的政策已經愈來愈多。近期對 [Medicaid](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/how-people-with-disabilities-will-bear-the-burden-of-medicaid-funding-cuts) 的刪減，將對身心障礙者造成不成比例的衝擊；而最近一項鼓勵將有心理健康障礙的[無家者機構化安置](https://www.urban.org/urban-wire/new-trump-policies-targeting-homelessness-threaten-rights-people-disabilities)的總統[行政命令](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/07/ending-crime-and-disorder-on-americas-streets/)，也會加速把身心障礙者送進機構，而不是協助我們取得住房與照護方案。此外，川普政府正[著手修訂規則](https://www.propublica.org/article/trump-social-security-ssi-disability-benefits-cuts-parents-children?utm_source=sailthru&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=majorinvestigations&utm_content=feature)，可能大幅削減或完全終止低收入補充保障收入（Supplemental Security Income, SSI）領取者的給付，嚴重傷害與低收入親屬同住在家中的身心障礙者。

[閱讀完整評論文章。](https://www.disabilityculturelab.org/posts/from-inside-the-house-how-surveillance-tech-further-threatens-independent-living)
